ev.q: CDC was notified of 12 cases of Legionnaires disease among travelers on two cruise ships
L. pneumophila serogroup 2–14 (Lp2–14) and non- pneumophila Legionella species were detected in six of 10 hot tubs.
No lower respiratory specimens were available; six patients were hospitalized, and no patients died.
four had concentrations of Legionella >100 colony-forming units (CFU)/mL, and two had concentrations >1,000 CFU/mL.

public_health_question.v: What was the source of on-board exposure in two cruise ship outbreaks of Legionnaires disease?

ev.q: CDC, in collaboration with the cruise lines, initiated investigations to ascertain the potential sources of on-board exposure
Two Outbreaks of Legionnaires Disease Associated with Outdoor Hot Tubs for Private Use
Two Outbreaks of Legionnaires Disease Associated with Outdoor Hot Tubs for Private Use — Two Cruise Ships
Local health departments interviewed patients to identify potential exposures on and off the ship
CDC reviewed the vessel’s Legionella environmental sampling results from the preceding 6 months and water management program records.
CDC published two Epidemic Information Exchange (Epi-X) calls for cases

equity.level_reason: Age and sex appear only as descriptive Table characteristics of cases; no social-position framing.

level_alternative.reason: U.S. residency of cases could be read as a nativity-type descriptor.

notes: Descriptive outbreak case series (12 cases) with environmental sampling counts; ship A and B characteristics are set side by side in the Table without any comparison claimed. Setting follows the single-site rule (ships as US subnational), although ship B's itineraries included Europe and two of its four patients were not U.S. residents.
